analysis.title: What's Trending Across Credit
key_insights: The AI trade's debate has shifted from how much capital will be deployed to how much financing the market can absorb, who bears the risk, and whether the economics justify the investment.
Pressure moved up the capital structure last week from neoclouds to hyperscalers, where strong operating results were overshadowed by large capex plans and a crowded financing pipeline.
GS 30Y hyperscaler basket widened 17bps on the week and is 85bps cheap to IG100 ex-hyperscalers. HY AI-related spreads widened 78bps over two weeks versus 22bps for non-AI HY excluding CCCs.

Oil above $100, Middle East tensions, European sovereign stress and rates volatility add pressure, but the market is not indiscriminately risk-off. Generic IG is resilient, BB credit draws demand and well-structured new issues clear.

IG spreads widened about 5bps on the week, but weakness is concentrated in hyperscalers, crowded TMT exposures and select European financials. Money centers, non-AI industrials and energy held in better.
TMT weakness reflects the absence of natural buyers more than outright selling. Investors are waiting for primary issuance rather than buying in the secondary market.

IG primary: $24.6bn priced across 14 deals, about 65% of issuance inside seven years. Average spread tightening from IPTs was 26.6bps, books 3.1x covered, average new-issue concession 4.1bps. Walmart and Kimberly-Clark benefited from demand for diversification away from AI supply.

October IG supply is near $71bn against a $130bn Street estimate. Possible additional hyperscaler deals come as European credit faces political and sovereign pressure, limiting an alternative outlet for USD supply.

HY spreads widened about 6bps, but the index masks three markets: resilient generic credit, an AI universe repricing, and low-quality issuers under severe stress. About 40% of HY bonds trade inside +200bps, AI-related HY is near +400bps, and CCC spreads reached about +1,127bps, a four-year wide.

Nearly 90% of CCC bonds by notional declined over 60 days, with daily moves 3.3x those of BBs. The 20 worst CCC bonds fell an average 14.3pts in October, nearly half of the bucket's total point losses. 59% of the HY market reports earnings by end of November.

JetBlue loyalty bonds fell more than 30pts over nine sessions to the low $40s and recovered to about $44.5 by Friday. The move reflected sentiment, systematic selling and thin liquidity rather than a single catalyst. Alaska and WestJet loans fell about 4.5pts and 9pts on the week on rising jet fuel costs.

CDX IG and HY ended the week near recent wides on AI credit stress, oil and European political uncertainty. Generic IG synthetics were insulated while HY, CCCs and AI-exposed single names absorbed more pressure.

Crude above $100/bbl on Strait of Hormuz tensions supported energy credit. Treasuries rallied and the 10Y briefly traded through 5% before strong flash PMI selling-price data challenged the move. The market is caught between growth concerns and inflation pressure ahead of the FOMC.

French political unrest and sovereign spread widening weighed on European financials and credit sentiment. A less accommodating European issuance window could leave more financing to clear in the US as the AI supply pipeline builds.

Equity hedge funds are cutting gross exposure aggressively and systematic rates strategies are heavily short duration. GS estimates bond CTAs are short about $145mm DV01 globally, so a yield decline could force short covering.

GS desks see hedge funds had their largest weekly de-grossing since July and systematic long/short had its worst week since 2024. The GS Momentum basket has had 30 daily moves of 5% or more this year, a record. BG leans toward later innings of a positioning unwind rather than the start of a longer AI repricing.

HF gross leverage remains 312% (96th percentile). CTA modeled S&P selling is $11.6bn in a flat week and up to $65bn in a one-month selloff. The desk sees potential for a relief rally if earnings stabilize sentiment but favors defined-risk upside exposure.

GS Mortgage desk sees value in non-QM RMBS AAA at +155-160bps over Treasuries, about 30bps wider since July, with 2-3yr base-case WAL. In agency MBS it prefers FN 5.0s-5.5s strategically, with tactical opportunities in FN 2.0s-2.5s.

tension_points.bull_case: Operating results are strong, well-structured new issues are clearing, and the desk sees the next financing clearing event as a sentiment catalyst once the concession is paid.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex plans and a crowded pipeline, including potential Meta and SpaceX supply, may outpace investor willingness to absorb issuance, with limited natural buyers and a narrowing European outlet.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A poorly received hyperscaler new issue requiring a large concession, or heavy supply arriving before the market stabilizes.

tension_points.bull_case: BG leans toward later innings of a positioning unwind, and the desk sees a possible relief rally if earnings stabilize sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage remains elevated and crowded CTA positioning leaves downside risk, with up to $65bn of modeled S&P selling in a one-month selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Mega-cap tech earnings that fail to stabilize sentiment.
